title: Improvement Registry shard-write + deterministic compaction transaction
problem_or_opportunity: The monolithic registry is unsafe for concurrent whole-file writes. The current family pointer solved visibility of extensions but still needs a canonical shard-write transaction and reproducible compaction path.
proposed_mechanism: Use candidate shards as the concurrent write surface; validate unique IDs across family; update family index with stale-write protection; periodically compile base+extensions into deterministic canonical JSON plus manifest of input SHAs/count/output SHA, readback and rollback snapshot.
expected_benefit: Reduces lost-update risk, avoids risky reconstruction of a minified monolith, and makes registry compaction auditable/reversible.
pilot_evidence: Current SI-0008 extension demonstrates shard visibility without rewriting base
Sprint 2 N31/N32 analysis selected shard+index and deterministic compaction
red_team_findings: Family index update itself must use stale-write/rebase semantics
Compactor must not silently override duplicate IDs
Compacted monolith is a build/read model, not proof that candidates are promoted
next_action: Implement unique-ID concurrency fixture and deterministic compaction builder with roundtrip/readback regression.
notes: Bounded pilot; current registry-family architecture stays CURRENT until candidate proves safe.
